newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine says to sell 4.33 tonnes of germanium.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says to sell 4.33 tonnes of germanium.

text.p: A Ukrainian rare metals plant will sell 4.33 tonnes of germanium over an unspecified time, the Ukrinform state news agency said on Thursday.
The agency's weekly Business News magazine reported that the Zaporizhya titanium-magnesium plant would sell the germanium from government reserves to raise money for modernisation.
It said the germanium was left over after an August sale of 6.5 tonnes, valued at $10.5 million, to three unnamed foreign companies.
Two of the companies, which won tenders to purchase and re-sell the metal in the August sale, had failed to find buyers for the 4.33 tonnes they had contracted for, it said.
"It is possible that two companies until this time have not sold their germanium due to unfavourable market prices," the report said.
"In this case Zaporizhya will have a additional tender for the right to sell the remaining germanium - around 4.33 tonnes."
Germanium, a by-product of zinc and copper ores, is used in high-frequency and high-power electronic applications such as infra-red systems, fibre optics and semi-conductors.
Western traders in September expressed nervousness that Ukraine had sold 6.5 tonnes of stockpiled material, fearing further price gyrations.
The Zaporizhya plant requires approximately $15 million for its 12-month upgrade programme.
